title: Perfect tensor quotient coaugmentation and its completion diagrams
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative complete discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$, where complete means that $R\to\varprojlim_{j\geq1}R/(\pi^j)$ is an isomorphism. Put $A_j=R/(\pi^j)$. Let $P,Q$ be bounded cochain complexes of finitely generated projective $R$-modules, representing perfect objects of $D(R)$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. With signed total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] put $V=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RQ)$ and
$$ U_j=(P\otimes_RA_j)\otimes_{A_j}(Q\otimes_RA_j). $$
Totalization is understood in this formula. Use the strict quotient transitions and the functorial shifted-cone model $H(U)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-t:\prod_jU_j\to\prod_jU_j)[-1]$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], applied to the one-point ringed site. Order its degree-$q$ coordinates as $(x,y)\in(\prod_jU_j)^q\oplus(\prod_jU_j)^{q-1}$, with differential $d(x,y)=(dx,(1-t)x-dy)$. Let $e_{P,Q}:V\to H(U)$ be the chain map whose first product coordinate sends $x\otimes y$ to $((x\bmod\pi^j)\otimes(y\bmod\pi^j))_j$ and whose shifted-product coordinate is zero.
Then $V$ is bounded finite projective, $U_j$ is canonically $V\otimes_RA_j$ by $(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes b)\mapsto(x\otimes y)\otimes ab$, and $e_{P,Q}$ is a quasi-isomorphism. More precisely, the quotient tower is termwise surjective, its termwise inverse limit is $V$ with these quotient projections, and $1-t$ is degreewise surjective with that kernel. In $D(R)$ this is the canonical completion isomorphism of the ordinary derived module tensor, natural in the two perfect objects and independent of bounded projective models.
Its quotient-coordinate formula intertwines the associator for three perfect complexes, the degree-$(i,j)$ Koszul symmetry, both multiplication unitors and the coefficient unit. It is compatible with every further quotient $A_m\to A_n$ for $m\geq n\geq1$. For a continuous local finite free homomorphism of complete discrete valuation rings $R\to S$, it is also compatible with extension of $P,Q$ to $S$, the balanced scalar tensorator, and the canonical completion comparisons. Here the $\pi$-power filtration on $S$ and the uniformizer-power filtration on $S$ are compared by their cofinal quotient maps; the assertion concerns the induced derived completion maps. The identity and iterated-extension squares commute, with the same quotient and zero shifted coordinates.
